findings.title: Caller-supplied source class can overstate a source prior
attack_path: A producer labels untrusted material as official_documentation.
The closed value passes structural validation.
Retrieval gives the record a small source-reliability advantage.
evidence: No source adapter authenticates the class.
The default source-reliability weight is limited to 0.03 and cannot change memory status.
findings.recommendation: Keep class caller-visible and low weight; require authenticated receipts before stronger trust treatment.

findings.title: Source class cannot confirm truth or grant runtime authority
attack_path: A record receives the highest source-class prior.
Its status, freshness, validity, contradictions, and capabilities remain unchanged.
Normal authorization and selection gates still apply.
evidence: The implementation reads source_class only during scoring and projection.
No permission, tool, skill, network, shell, or status write consumes source_class.
findings.recommendation: Review any future non-ranking consumer as a new trust boundary.

findings.title: Unknown source-class values fail at domain and database boundaries
attack_path: A producer submits an invented privileged class.
Python enum validation or SQLite CHECK rejects it.
The invalid value cannot enter normal retrieval.
evidence: Focused tests cover invalid Python and direct SQLite values.
findings.recommendation: Keep vocabulary changes versioned and explicit.

limitations: Source classification is not cryptographically authenticated.
Initial priors are not empirical truth probabilities.
No source-specific outcome calibration was available.
No external content, provider, network, shell, or skill execution is introduced.
